questions.q: What is a major distinction between a curtain wall and a loadbearing exterior wall?
o: It carries no floor or roof loads
It must be built of masonry
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - doors, windows, glazing and curtain-wall systems
questions.n: Curtain walls are non-loadbearing exterior enclosure systems supported by the building structure.

questions.q: What are the vertical framing members of a stile-and-rail door called?
questions.ref: Architectural Woodwork Institute (AWI), door and frame terminology
questions.n: Stiles are the vertical members of a stile-and-rail door assembly.

questions.q: What determines whether a glazing product may be used in a fire-rated opening?
o: Its tested and listed fire rating
questions.ref: NFPA 80 and listed fire-protection glazing requirements; UL fire-rated glazing listings
questions.n: Fire-rated glazing must be tested/listed for the required fire-protection or fire-resistance function and installed in an approved assembly.

questions.q: Which lock type is surface-mounted to the face of a door rather than installed into the door edge?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - glass, window, door and hardware terminology
questions.n: A rim lock is mounted on the surface of the door; mortise and cylindrical/unit locks are installed into bored or mortised portions of the door.

questions.q: Which glass treatment is specifically intended to reduce thermal infrared heat transfer while maintaining useful daylight?
questions.ref: Glass Association of North America (GANA), Glazing Manual / laminated and insulating glass guidance
questions.n: Low-e coatings reduce long-wave infrared radiative heat transfer across glazing systems.

questions.q: Which metal is traditionally deposited as the reflective layer in high-quality glass mirrors?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - glass, window, door and hardware terminology
questions.n: Modern glass mirrors traditionally use a silver reflective coating protected by backing layers.

questions.q: What is an individual piece of glass installed in a window, door, or curtain wall called?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - glass, window, door and hardware terminology
questions.n: A lite is an individual pane or piece of glass within a frame or glazing assembly.

questions.q: What interlayer material is most commonly associated with laminated architectural safety glass?
questions.ref: ASTM C1172 - Standard Specification for Laminated Architectural Flat Glass
questions.n: PVB is a widely used polymer interlayer in laminated architectural glazing.

questions.q: A warehouse opening uses horizontal steel slats that rise vertically and coil above the opening. What door type is this?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - glass, window, door and hardware terminology
questions.n: Interlocking slats guided at the sides and coiled around an overhead drum identify a rolling door.

questions.q: For substantially improved sound reduction in a sealed opening, which general glazing strategy is usually more effective than a single thin monolithic lite?
questions.ref: Glass Association of North America (GANA), Glazing Manual / laminated and insulating glass guidance
questions.n: Laminated interlayers and separated panes can improve sound transmission loss, especially when glass thicknesses and air spaces are appropriately selected.

questions.q: Which curtain-wall system is assembled largely on site from individual mullions, rails, and glazing components?
questions.ref: Fenestration and Glazing Industry Alliance (FGIA), curtain-wall and fenestration terminology
questions.n: Stick curtain walls are assembled piece-by-piece at the building from vertical mullions, horizontal rails, glazing, and related components.

questions.q: What is the principal thermal purpose of the sealed cavity in an IGU?
o: To eliminate the need for frames
To reduce heat transfer through the glazing
To act as a structural column
questions.ref: Glass Association of North America (GANA), Glazing Manual / laminated and insulating glass guidance
questions.n: The sealed air or gas space improves thermal resistance compared with a single monolithic lite.

questions.q: In older glazing terminology, approximately what thickness is associated with single-strength glass?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - glass, window, door and hardware terminology
questions.n: Traditional trade terminology commonly associates single-strength window glass with roughly 2.5 mm thickness.

questions.q: What type of large metal door opens by coiling interlocking horizontal slats around an overhead drum?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - glass, window, door and hardware terminology
questions.n: A rolling door is made of interlocking slats that travel in side guides and coil around an overhead barrel or drum.

questions.q: An exterior facade is built by installing vertical mullions first, then horizontal rails and glass panels one component at a time. Which curtain-wall method is being used?
questions.ref: Fenestration and Glazing Industry Alliance (FGIA), curtain-wall and fenestration terminology
questions.n: Piece-by-piece field assembly of mullions, rails, and glazing identifies a stick system.

questions.q: What is the principal raw material used to supply silica in ordinary soda-lime architectural glass?
questions.ref: ASTM C1036 - Standard Specification for Flat Glass
questions.n: Silica sand is the primary source of silica in conventional soda-lime-silica flat glass.

questions.q: Which of these is typically classified as a coated architectural glass product?
o: Plain float glass with no treatment
questions.ref: Glass Association of North America (GANA), Glazing Manual / laminated and insulating glass guidance
questions.n: Self-cleaning glazing uses a functional surface coating designed to aid breakdown and removal of organic dirt.

questions.q: Why must curtain-wall attachments accommodate building-frame movement?
o: So it can carry the floor loads
So frame drift and heat do not damage it
So every panel is locked rigid
So no joints are needed at all
questions.ref: Fenestration and Glazing Industry Alliance (FGIA), curtain-wall and fenestration terminology
questions.n: Curtain-wall anchors and joints must accommodate interstory drift, deflection, and thermal movement while maintaining enclosure performance.

questions.q: In older glazing terminology, approximately what thickness is associated with double-strength glass?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - glass, window, door and hardware terminology
questions.n: Traditional trade terminology commonly associates double-strength window glass with roughly 3 mm thickness.

questions.q: What manufacturing method revolutionized modern flat-glass production by forming a continuous ribbon on molten tin?
questions.ref: Pilkington / glass-industry technical histories of the float glass process
questions.n: The float process forms molten glass into a flat ribbon by floating it on a bath of molten tin.

questions.q: What is a key safety benefit of laminated glass after breakage?
o: Fragments tend to remain adhered to the interlayer
It separates into loose sharp shards immediately
questions.ref: ASTM C1172 - Standard Specification for Laminated Architectural Flat Glass
questions.n: The interlayer helps retain broken glass fragments, reducing fallout and maintaining a residual barrier.

questions.q: What is the narrow glazed panel located immediately beside a door called?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - doors, windows, glazing and curtain-wall systems
questions.n: A sidelight is a narrow glazed opening or panel adjacent to a doorway.

questions.q: A safety-glazing panel must remain largely held together after fracture. Which glass type best fits that requirement?
questions.ref: ASTM C1172 - Standard Specification for Laminated Architectural Flat Glass
questions.n: The bonded interlayer in laminated glass retains many broken fragments after impact.

questions.q: Which assembly consists of two or more panes separated by a sealed air or gas space?
questions.ref: Glass Association of North America (GANA), Glazing Manual / laminated and insulating glass guidance
questions.n: An IGU uses multiple glass lites separated by a sealed spacer system and cavity.

questions.q: Which category best describes reflective architectural glass?
questions.ref: Glass Association of North America (GANA), Glazing Manual / laminated and insulating glass guidance
questions.n: Reflective glass obtains its solar-control appearance and performance from a surface coating.

questions.q: Which hinge type allows a door to swing in both directions and return toward a closed position by gravity?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - glass, window, door and hardware terminology
questions.n: Double-acting gravity hinges are used for doors that swing both ways and return by gravity.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a drip groove or capillary break at the lower edge of a sash?
o: To remove the need for weatherstrips
To lock the sash in place
To stop water tracking to the inside
questions.ref: FGIA/AAMA window and curtain-wall water-management guidance
questions.n: Drip edges and capillary breaks interrupt surface-tension paths and help prevent water from tracking inward.

questions.q: Which product is not inherently a fire-rated glazing material merely because of its surface treatment?
questions.ref: NFPA 80 and listed fire-protection glazing requirements; UL fire-rated glazing listings
questions.n: Ceramic frit is a surface treatment; fire resistance/protection depends on the glazing product and its tested/listed assembly, not fritting alone.

questions.q: What is a vertical member separating adjacent window or door units?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - doors, windows, glazing and curtain-wall systems
questions.n: A mullion is a vertical or horizontal framing member dividing adjacent window or door units.
